target_customer: Brazilian and Mexican ride-hailing and delivery app drivers who want to rent or lease-to-own a car without a credit check.
problem: Only about 20 percent of Brazilians own a car and traditional rental companies serve only 20 to 30 percent of roughly 1 million app drivers, leaving many without access to a vehicle.
business_model: Car rental and subscription for app drivers, asset-light fleet sourced from automakers and rental firms, with a purchase option

founders.name: Adhemar Milani Neto
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch and Contxto describe him as a former 99 executive.

founders.name: Joao Costa
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO in TechCrunch, LatamList and Contxto; the YC page lists only Milani.

competitors.name: Localiza, Unidas and Movida
competitors.what: Large traditional rental companies buying cars at scale and renting for 12 to 18 months before resale, also serving app drivers
competitors.traction_then: Serve roughly 20 to 30 percent of Brazil's 1 million app drivers

technical_complexity.rationale: Fleet operations, telematics, maintenance logistics and pricing across cities are operationally hard rather than research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Asset-light sourcing and data on driver behavior helped, but rental incumbents had cheaper capital and scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept competing; Kovi planned an IPO but instead was acquired by Moove in an all-share deal announced January 29, 2025.

market_need_then: Few Brazilians owned cars, the number of app drivers was large and expected to double within five years per the CEO, and many drivers were underserved by traditional rental firms.

branding.domain_note: Uses kovi.com.br, a Brazilian ccTLD domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Inclusive, driver-focused; tagline 'O carro que todos podem escolher' and driver testimonials on the site.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline about a car everyone can choose, with no credit check
branding.community_and_virality: Site features driver testimonials; no source on merch or fan activity.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among Brazilian app drivers and in LatAm startup press, with a retained brand after the Moove deal, but no source on brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Kovi was founded in August 2018 by two ex-99 executives, raised a $10.5M seed in May 2019, a $30M Series A in November 2019 and a $104M Series B in August 2021 with Valor and Prosus, and grew to 12,000 cars by then. Capital-heavy rental and growth of Moove's global fleet led to an all-share sale to Moove in January 2025 at an undisclosed price. Later conflicting valuation estimates are unverified.
notes: No Series C found. Series B total equity since inception reported as about $145M. Moove deal was subject to Brazilian antitrust approval per some reports; one outlet says finalized; closing date not found, so 2025-01 is the announcement month. Kovi's TechCabal page returned 403. Aggregator valuations (Dealroom $500M to 1B, $629.6M estimate) are unverified and not recorded. The debt facility date is the Series B article date. No source explains the name Kovi; marked invented from form only.
